title: Nat20Api
description: Schema root: every type that crosses the wire. Exported by `export-schema`; not itself sent.

oneOf.description: Strength.
Dexterity.
Constitution.
Intelligence.
Wisdom.
Charisma.

save_bonus.description: Saving throw bonus: what the engine adds to the d20, without dice bonuses such as Bless.

save_proficient.description: Whether the creature is proficient in this saving throw.

spell_slot.description: Spell slot level spent, for spells.

ActionOption.description: One option the actor can take at the pending prompt.

action.description: The engine action id behind the option.

area.description:
The area it fills, for an option whose `targeting` is `area`, with whom each aim would
catch.

item.description: The carried item this option uses up, for a potion. Its option id is `use/<item>`.

max_targets.description:
How many targets `submit` may name: 0 for `none`, `self`, `point` and `area`, 1 for
`single`.

range_ft.description: Range in feet, when the option has one.

spell.description:
The spell this option casts, for a spell. Its option id is `cast/<spell>/<slot level>`,
or `cast/<spell>` for a cantrip.

summary.description:
What the option does, in one to three plain sentences: the rule's own short text from the
engine, the same for every viewer. It never carries a DC, odds or a computed number. Absent
when the rule has none (a monster's own attacks).

targets.description: Creatures the option can target, with their distance.

variants.description: Variants `submit` must pick from, e.g. a spell's casting level. Empty when none.

AdvantageState.description: Advantage state of a d20 roll.

oneOf.description: One d20.
Two d20s, keep the higher.
Two d20s, keep the lower.

Against.description: The number a roll was compared with.

oneOf.description: Armor Class.
Difficulty Class.

Aim.description:
Where an area is aimed: its centre, or for an area that starts at the actor, the direction it
points.

oneOf.description: At a creature, where it stands.
At a named landmark the scene defines.
At an exact point.

AnchorObserved.description: A named landmark as one player sees it: the DM's view plus how far away it is.

distance_ft.description: Straight-line distance from the viewer's creature, in feet.

id.description: Anchor id from the scene, the `anchor` a `move` names.

name.description: What the characters call it, e.g. "the mill gate".

AnchorView.description: A named landmark as the DM sees it.

id.description: Anchor id from the scene, the `anchor` a `move` names.

name.description: What the characters call it, e.g. "the mill gate".

hint.description: What the caller can do instead, when the engine knows.

message.description:
One plain sentence written for a model or a human. Never Rust debug output, and never a
number the request's `viewer` may not see (CLAUDE.md Rule 3).

reason.description: Finer reason for `rejected`; absent for other codes.

retryable.description: Whether the same request can succeed after the caller changes its input or waits.

AreaAim.description: One aim of an area option and the creatures it would catch.

catches.description: The creatures the area would catch, the actor's allies included, by handle.

oneOf.description: A cone, e.g. Burning Hands.
A sphere.
A cube.
A cylinder.
A line.

Awaiting.description: Who the engine waits on next, tagged by `kind`.

oneOf.description: A creature's turn: `legal_actions`, then `submit`, `move` or `end_turn`.
A creature may react to a trigger: answer with `react`.
Nothing pending: explore mode, or a session with no scene yet.

A character's level-up is open, out of combat: its player answers the choice that
`level_up` or the last `answer_level_up` returned (protocol §4.14). The choice itself
goes only to that player.

Combat ended by itself because a side is down. The scene is already back in explore mode
and nothing is pending. Reported until a command changes the session (`load_scene`,
`start_combat`, or any explore command that acts), after which it reads `none`; read-only
and rejected commands keep reporting it.
Go on with any explore command, `start_combat` or `load_scene`; `end_combat` is not needed.

winner.description: The side left standing, if any.

oneOf.description: No session: call `new_session`.

CaravanView.description: The caravan. Every player sees it.

owner.description:
Who owns it and decides where it goes: a player's handle, or `npc:<id>` for a world NPC
that follows the campaign's route.

CardChoiceView.description: One choice on a road card.

id.description: The choice id; `choose_card` takes it.

CardDecided.description: How a road card was decided.

oneOf.description: The player owner chose, after the Blades' advice.
The Blades' majority.
A tie, broken by the human seat (Blade cards) or the card's own pick.
The NPC owner insisted on a choice; the DM narrates why.
Nobody could speak; the card's default.

CardDm.description: The road card on the table, as the DM sees it.

id.description: The card id in the world's deck.

said.description: What each Blade has said so far.

waiting_for.description: The Blades who still have to speak.

zone.description: The deck zone it came from: a road zone or a place id.

CardPlayer.description: The road card on the table, as a player sees it: no card id, zone or deck.

said.description: What each Blade has said so far.

waiting_for.description: The Blades who still have to speak.

CardSaid.description: One seat's word on the card on the table: a Blade's advice or vote.

oneOf.description:
The road, the wagons, the cargo: the caravan owner decides after every Hired Blade
advises; an NPC owner takes the Blades' majority.
The escort themselves: the Hired Blades vote.

CargoView.description: Some of one good in a wagon.

weight_lb.description: The weight of all of them, in pounds.

CarriedItem.description: Some of one item a creature carries.

item.description: The item's id, as on a sheet (`potion_of_healing`).

oneOf.description:
A check the scenario defines, with its skill or saving throw and its DC. Rolled at most
once per scene.

A check the DM picks from the SRD DC ladder (5 very easy to 30 nearly impossible) when no
scenario check fits. Not limited per scene.

ability.description: The ability; it must be the skill's own ability.

dc.description: The DC: one of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30; anything else is a `bad_request`.

skill.description: The skill. A check without one answers `not_implemented`.

oneOf.description: An ability check with a skill, e.g. Wisdom (Insight).

skill.description: The skill; its ability is the SRD default.

oneOf.description: A saving throw.

CheckView.description: A scenario check as the DM sees it.

id.description: Check id from the scene.

rolled.description: Whether the check was already rolled in this scene; it cannot be rolled again.

ClockView.description: The world's time. The one calendar: core keeps time inside a fight by turns.

day.description: The day of the campaign, from 1.

minute.description: The minute of the hour, 0 to 59.

Coins.description:
Coins by denomination (SRD 5.2.1: 1 PP = 10 GP, 1 GP = 10 SP = 100 CP, 1 EP = 50 CP). In a
request a denomination left out is 0.

oneOf.description: Every creature on one side is down.
The DM ended it: the other side surrendered.
The DM ended it: the other side fled.
A scenario trigger ended it.

CommandResult.description:
The typed result of each command, tagged by `cmd`.

Variants are struct variants, never newtype variants: schemars renders a tagged newtype variant
as `$ref` plus sibling keywords, which the TS generator drops, losing the tag.

oneOf.description: What the engine says about itself on `hello`.

engine_rev.description: The `nat20_core` revision the engine was built against.

schema_sha256.description:
SHA-256 over `generated/nat20-api.schema.json` followed by `generated/nat20-scene.schema.json`.
Clients compare it with the hash they were generated from.

oneOf.description: The new session.

seed.description: The dice seed in use, given or picked.

oneOf.description: The state after the scene loaded.
The current state.
A full sheet.
The actor's options at the pending prompt.

budget.description:
What the actor has left of its turn, in combat mode. Absent in explore mode, where
there is no turn.

can_end_turn.description: Whether `end_turn` is accepted now; always false in explore mode.

options.description: Options the actor can take now.

prompt_id.description:
The prompt these options belong to; echo it in `submit` and `end_turn`. Empty in
explore mode, where nothing is pending.

unavailable.description: Options the actor has but cannot take now, with the reason.

oneOf.description: The option was taken; its rolls and effects are in `events`.
The reaction was taken or declined; its rolls and effects are in `events`.
The turn ended; the next prompt is in `awaiting`.
The move happened.

moved_ft.description:
Distance moved by the time of the response, in feet; less than the route while an
opportunity attack holds the creature where it provoked, or when the attack stopped it.

provoked.description: Creatures that got an opportunity attack prompt from this move, in prompt order.

reached.description:
Whether the walk set out to end where the creature was sent (next to the creature, at
the anchor or the point). False only for a `partial` move that the movement left cut
short; a creature an opportunity attack holds on the way is still on a walk that
reaches.

oneOf.description: The check's roll and outcome.

success.description: Whether the check succeeded. The engine decides, never the caller.

oneOf.description: Hit Points regained on the short rest.

healed.description:
One entry per participant, in `participants` order; `amount` is 0 for one that spent
no dice. Each die's roll and `healed` event are in `events`.

oneOf.description: The state after initiative, in combat mode.
The state after combat ended, in explore mode.
The state after the spawn.
The help was given; what it rolled and changed is in `events`.
The goods changed hands; the `ledger` entry is in `events`.
The theft's roll and outcome.

roll_id.description: The Sleight of Hand roll, also in `events`.

success.description: Whether the goods were taken unseen. The engine decides, never the caller.

oneOf.description: What was taken is in `events`: one `ledger` entry for the coins and one per item.
The state after initiative, in combat mode.
The state after the creature is placed.
The state with the world in it.
The state after the word, with the card gone once it was decided.
The saved party.

roster.description: Write it to a file as is; `new_session{roster}` reads it back.

oneOf.description: The level-up's first open choice, or none when core needed no answer from the player.

choice.description: The choice to answer with `answer_level_up`; absent once the level-up is done.

oneOf.description: The next open choice of the level-up, or none once it is done.

choice.description: The choice to answer next; absent once the level-up is done.

oneOf.description: The night and the state at dawn.

night.description: The night, also in the `night` event.

oneOf.description: The leg and the state after it, in the scene the leg ended in.

leg.description: The leg, also in the `traveled` event.

oneOf.description: Log entries after `since`.

events.description: Projected for the request's `viewer`. Entries the viewer may not see are left out.

next.description: Pass as `since` to read on from here.

oneOf.description: The caster started concentrating on another spell.
The caster failed the Constitution save after taking damage.
The caster was incapacitated or died.
The spell's duration ran out.
Anything else, such as the caster ending it.

Condition.description: The SRD 5.2.1 conditions (Exhaustion is a level on the sheet, not listed here).

oneOf.description: Blinded.
Charmed.
Deafened.
Frightened.
Grappled.
Incapacitated.
Invisible.
Paralyzed.
Petrified.
Poisoned.
Prone.
Restrained.
Stunned.
Unconscious.

CreatureFull.description: A creature as its owner and the DM see it.

concentration.description: The spell it is concentrating on, if any.

conditions.description:
Active conditions, by name. A creature at 0 Hit Points that is not dead is
`unconscious`.

effects.description:
Lasting effects on it that run out or end, such as Bless or a Help's Advantage, in the
order they began. Owner and DM only: other players learn of them from the table.

health.description: The health band other players see.

CreatureObserved.description: A creature as another player perceives it. Has no Hit Points, Armor Class or stat block, by design.

distance_ft.description: Distance from the viewer, in feet.

oneOf.description: Acid.
Bludgeoning.
Cold.
Fire.
Force.
Lightning.
Necrotic.
Piercing.
Poison.
Psychic.
Radiant.
Slashing.
Thunder.
The scenario file.
The SRD DC ladder, picked by the DM.
A stat block.

A rule of the game: the DC 10 of a death save, or of the Medicine check of a Help that
stabilizes; a Concentration save's DC (10 or half the damage taken).

The caster's spell save DC (8 + spellcasting ability modifier + Proficiency Bonus): a
spell's save, or a class feature that uses it, such as Divine Spark.
The target's passive score, as core computes it: passive Perception against a theft.

DiceRolled.description: One group of dice in a roll.

kept.description: The sum the roll kept, after Advantage or Disadvantage.

results.description: Every die's face, including dropped ones.

source.description: What the dice are for, e.g. `d20` or `longsword`.

EffectLine.description: A lasting effect on a creature.

id.description: Effect id from the registry with `/` for dots, e.g. `spell/bless`, `help/attack_roll`.

source.description: The creature whose action put it there: the creature itself for its own Dash or Rage.

EncounterView.description: A scene encounter as the DM sees it.

id.description: Encounter id from the scene, the `encounter_id` a `start_combat` names.

running.description: Whether this encounter is the fight running now.

surrender_available.description:
Whether `end_combat{surrender}` would be accepted now: the encounter is running and its
surrender condition holds (decision D5). The engine works this out; the DM decides
whether to call it.

surrendering.description:
The creatures that `end_combat{surrender}` would make `neutral` now: the surrender
condition's creatures still conscious, in the condition's order. Empty, and left out,
unless `surrender_available`. A creature of the fight that the condition doesn't name
(a wolf beside surrendering goblins) is never here and fights on.

EndCombatReason.description: Why the DM ends combat early.

oneOf.description:
The encounter's surrender condition holds and the DM calls the surrender. Its surrendering
creatures that are still conscious become `neutral` and stay in the scene.

The other side fled; the encounter must list `fled` in its `end_reasons`. Its conscious
creatures leave the scene and the party's side wins.
The story ends the fight; the encounter must list `scenario` in its `end_reasons`.

EquipSlot.description: Where an item is worn or wielded.

oneOf.description: Body armour.
A melee weapon in the main hand; a two-handed weapon takes both hands.
A melee weapon in the off hand.
A ranged weapon in the main hand.
A ranged weapon in the off hand.
Malformed JSON, a missing or wrongly typed field, or an unknown `cmd`.
`v` is not a version this engine speaks.
The command needs a session and none exists.
The command needs a loaded scene and none is loaded.
The creature handle is not in this scene.
The option id is not offered by the current prompt.
The check id is not defined by the scene.
The anchor id is not defined by the scene.
The spawn id is not declared by the scene.
The encounter id is not declared by the scene.
`place_creature` names a stat block the registry doesn't have.
A world command (`travel`) before `start_campaign`.
The actor is not the one the engine is waiting on.
The prompt id does not match the pending prompt.
The viewer may not see what it asked for.
A combat command in explore mode, or the reverse.
The engine refused a well-formed decision; see `reason`.

`end_combat{surrender}` while the running encounter's surrender condition does not hold,
or for an encounter that declares none. Nothing changed. Not retryable as it stands; the
condition may hold later in the fight.
The command is in the contract but this engine build does not implement it yet.
The scene file, or a pregen or stat block it names, is missing or invalid. Nothing changed.

`new_session` with a roster this engine cannot read (another format, a pregen it has no
file for), or a scene whose roster character cannot be rebuilt. Nothing changed.
An engine bug. The request did nothing; details go to stderr.

ErrorHint.description: What the caller can do instead of the failed request.

awaiting.description: The pending prompt, e.g. with the current `prompt_id` after `stale_prompt`.

known_ids.description:
The ids the scene does define, after an unknown id (`unknown_anchor`, `unknown_check`,
`unknown_encounter`). Sent to the DM only, because ids are scenario data.

legal_option_ids.description: Option ids the actor can take at the pending prompt.

EscortBlade.description: One Hired Blade's service and pay.

served.description: Days served: one for each night they lived through, and the day of arrival.

EscortDm.description: The escort contract as the DM sees it.

contract.description: The terms and each Blade's service and pay, as the players see them.

purse_cp.description: What the merchant's purse holds now, in copper pieces.

EscortView.description: The escort contract as the party knows it: the terms, and each Blade's days and pay.

advance_days.description: Days of wages paid ahead when the contract started.

destination.description: Where the caravan is escorted to; the rest of the pay is due on arrival.

done.description: Whether the caravan reached the destination and the pay was settled.

wage_cp.description: The wage per Blade per day, in copper pieces.

round.description: The combat round, in combat mode.

scene.description: The scene the event happened in; absent before the first scene loads.

seq.description: Position in the session log, from 1. Unique and monotonic for the whole session.

text.description: One plain sentence rendered for the viewer. Never carries a number the viewer may not see.

oneOf.description: The session started.
A scene loaded.

mode.description: The mode the scene starts in.

oneOf.description: Initiative was rolled; combat started.

participants.description: Every creature in the fight, in initiative order.

oneOf.description:
Creatures surrendered: the DM called the surrender while their encounter allowed it. They
are now `neutral` and stay in the scene.

handles.description: The creatures that surrendered, in the encounter's order.

oneOf.description:
Creatures fled: the DM ended the fight with `end_combat{fled}` while their encounter
allowed it. They have left the scene; creatures of their side at 0 Hit Points stay where
they fell.

handles.description: The creatures that fled, in scene order.

oneOf.description: Combat ended.

winner.description: The side left standing, if any.

oneOf.description: A new combat round started.
A creature's turn started.
A creature's turn ended.
A creature took an option.

A creature walked to reach the target of the option it submitted (one whose target was out
of reach or sight, protocol §4.4) and did not get to take it: an Opportunity Attack the walk
provoked dropped it or left it unable to move (§4.1), or the option could not be taken
where it ended.
Nothing the option costs is spent; the movement is. In a fight the creature's action prompt
stays open. Logged in place of the `action` it did not take.

option_id.description: The option it did not take.

oneOf.description: The engine rolled dice.

roll.description: The roll, in the view the viewer may see.

oneOf.description: A creature took damage. The amount is said at the table; the Hit Points left are not.

source_roll.description: The damage roll, when one was made.

oneOf.description: A creature regained Hit Points.

source_roll.description: The healing roll, when one was made.

oneOf.description: A creature's Hit Points changed. DM and owner only.
A condition started.

source.description: What caused it, e.g. a spell or feature id.

oneOf.description: A condition ended.
A caster started concentrating on a spell. Public: a caster visibly maintains a spell.

spell.description: The spell's id, as in the caster's `spells` (`bless`).

oneOf.description: A caster's concentration ended, and with it the spell's effects. Public.

spell.description: The spell's id, as in the caster's `spells` (`bless`).

oneOf.description:
A lasting effect began on a creature (Bless, a Help's Advantage, Rage). Owner and DM
only: the table hears the spell or action, not its numbers.

effect.description: The effect's id, as in `effects` on the sheet (`spell/bless`).

source.description: The creature whose action put it there.

oneOf.description:
A lasting effect on a creature ended: it ran out, was used, or its Concentration ended.
Owner and DM only.

effect.description: The effect's id, as in `effects` on the sheet (`spell/bless`).

oneOf.description:
A creature used up a carried item, e.g. drank a Potion of Healing or gave it to someone.
Public: it is seen at the table. Logged right after the `action` that used it.

item.description: The item's id, as on the sheet (`potion_of_healing`).

target.description: Who it was used on: the actor itself when drunk.

oneOf.description:
Coin or items changed hands: one entry of the ledger (`nat20-ledger`). Public, except a
theft, which only the thief and the DM see.

from.description: Who gave: a creature handle, or `npc:<id>`, `wagon:<n>`, `market:<place>`, `world`.

roll_id.description: The roll that decided it, for a theft.

to.description: Who received, in the same form.

oneOf.description: A theft failed: the target caught the thief, and nothing moved. Public.
A creature's life state changed.

A creature moved: by a `move`, or on its own on the way to an option's target (a
`submit` on a target out of reach, a scripted monster's approach), logged once it stopped
and before the `action` it walked for (protocol §4.1).

anchor.description: The anchor it moved to, when it moved to one and got there.

oneOf.description: A check resolved. DM only: `check_id` is scenario data.

check_id.description: The scenario check id, for scenario checks.

oneOf.description: A scene flag was set for the first time this session. DM only.

A scenario hazard was set off; its saving throw follows. DM only: players see the save
and any damage.

actor.description: The creature that set it off and makes the save.

oneOf.description: A rest finished, after any Hit Point Dice it spent; resources have recharged. Public.

Creatures were placed by a spawn: on `spawn`, or by the engine when a flag spawn's fight
starts or a round spawn's round comes. In a running fight their `initiative` rolls follow.
DM only, because the spawn id is scenario data; players see the creatures in
their state.

The DM placed a creature the scene file doesn't list (`place_creature`). DM only, like
`spawned`; players see the creature in their state. In a running fight its `initiative`
roll follows.

The caravan travelled one leg (`travel`). Public. On arrival `place_discovered` may
follow, then `scene_loaded` for the scene the leg ended in.

A road card was drawn after a leg or a night in camp (protocol §4.13). Public: the text
and choices only; the card id and the draw roll are DM-only. The card's own words are
`card_text`: a field named `text` here would clash with the event's own `text`, which the
variant is flattened into.

card_text.description: What the players read: the card's own words.

oneOf.description: A Hired Blade's advice on a caravan card or vote on a Blade card. Public.
The card on the table was decided; its effects follow in the log. Public.
A road card added or took goods from the caravan. Public.

A character gained Experience Points for a fight its side won (SRD 5.2.1: the XP of the
defeated foes, split evenly). Owner and DM only.

can_level_up.description: It has the points for its next level.

oneOf.description: A character reached a new level (`level_up`). Public.

A road card cost the party time: the clock moved on and the day's travel shrank.
Public.

The caravan reached the escort contract's destination and the Blades' pay was settled
(API-47), after its `wage` ledger entries. Public.

A night passed (`rest_night`), after its `ledger`, saving throw and `rest` entries.
Public.

The party found a place it did not know: it is in every player's `world.places` from
now on. Public.

Experience.description: A character's Experience Points (SRD 5.2.1, Character Advancement).

can_level_up.description:
The character has the points for its next level: its player may call `level_up` out of
combat.

next_level.description: The Experience Points the next level needs. Absent at level 20.

id.description: Feature id, e.g. `fighting_style.defense`.

oneOf.description: Coins.
One carried item, not one worn or wielded.

item.description: The item's id, as on the sheet (`potion_of_healing`).

Handle.description: A creature's handle in the session, e.g. `bren` or `goblin_1`. Stable for the creature's life.

HealthBand.description: Coarse health that every viewer may see. SRD 5.2.1: Bloodied means half Hit Points or fewer.

oneOf.description: More than half Hit Points.
Half Hit Points or fewer, above 0.
At 0 Hit Points or dead.

HelpSpec.description: What a `help` does (SRD 5.2.1, Rules Glossary, Help).

oneOf.description:
Gives `ally` Advantage on their next ability check with `skill`. The helper needs
proficiency in the skill (`rejected` / `not_proficient` otherwise). The benefit is spent by
that check and ends at the start of the helper's next turn; out of combat that is the
helper's first turn in a fight, or the next scene.

ally.description: The creature that gets Advantage; not the helper.

oneOf.description:
A DC 10 Wisdom (Medicine) check to make `target`, a creature at 0 Hit Points, Stable.
A target that is not dying answers `rejected` / `invalid_target`.

HitDicePool.description: Hit Point Dice of one size.

HitDiceSpend.description: Hit Point Dice one creature spends on a short rest.

count.description:
How many dice to spend. More than it has left answers `rejected` with
`insufficient_resource`. The largest die size it has left goes first; each die rolls
plus the Constitution modifier, and regains at least 1 Hit Point.

handle.description: The creature: one of the rest's participants, listed once.

equipped.description: Whether it is equipped or wielded.

id.description: Item id from the registry, e.g. `longsword`.

oneOf.description: Coins, as their worth in copper pieces.
Some of one item.

item.description: The item's id, as on the sheet.

LedgerReason.description: Why something moved in the ledger. A closed set.

oneOf.description: Handed over, bought or sold.
A Hired Blade's pay.
Taken from a fallen or surrendered creature.
A toll.
An inn's fee.
A theft that worked.
A reward.

LegView.description: One journey leg, in `travel`'s result and the `traveled` event.

arrived.description:
Whether the caravan reached the road's end; if not, it stopped on the road because the
day's distance is spent.

LevelUpChoice.description: One choice of a level-up, asked of the levelling creature's player only (protocol §4.14).

label.description: What is chosen, in plain words, e.g. "Spell Selection".

options.description: The options, in a stable order.

recommended.description:
The option ids recommended, as many as `picks`. An `answer_level_up` with no `picks`
takes them.

LevelUpOption.description: One option of a level-up choice.

id.description: Echo it in `answer_level_up.picks`, e.g. `hold_person` or `athletics`.

summary.description: One plain line on what it does, from the rules (a spell's own summary).

oneOf.description: Above 0 Hit Points.
At 0 Hit Points, making death saving throws.
At 0 Hit Points and stable.
Dead.

Lodging.description: Where the party spends a night.

oneOf.description:
The inn of the place the caravan is in: each party member pays the place's `inn_cp`
for room and board.

A camp, in a place or on the road: each party member eats one day's rations from the
caravan while they last.

MilesToday.description:
How many more miles the party can travel today at each pace. A day's distance is shared:
a mile at Fast spends 1/30 of the day, at Normal 1/24, at Slow 1/18.

fast.description: Miles left today at a Fast pace.

normal.description: Miles left today at a Normal pace.

slow.description: Miles left today at a Slow pace.

Mode.description: Whether the session is out of combat or in initiative order.

oneOf.description: Exploration and social play: no initiative, checks on request.
Initiative order: one actor at a time, reactions interrupt.

Modifier.description: One modifier added to a roll.

source.description: What it comes from, e.g. "Strength" or "Proficiency".

oneOf.description: A named landmark the scene defines, e.g. `millwheel`.
Within 5 feet of a creature.

handle.description: The creature to move next to.

oneOf.description: An exact point.

NightView.description: One night, in `rest_night`'s result and the `night` event.

hungry.description: The party members who ate less than a full day's food (no rations left).

minutes.description: How long the night lasted, in minutes: until dawn, and at least 8 hours.

not_rested.description:
The party members who could not take a Long Rest: at 0 Hit Points, or less than 16
hours after their last one.

rested.description: The party members who finished a Long Rest.

NpcAttitude.description: How a place NPC feels about the party.

oneOf.description: Glad of them.
Neither.
Against them: they stand on the hostile side of a fight.

NpcDm.description: A place NPC as the DM sees them (API-48).

attitude.description: How they feel about the party.

hp.description:
Hit Points when the party last left them; absent when at full. While the party is in
their place, their creature in the scene has the live value.

id.description: The id; also their creature handle while the party is in their place.

met.description: Whether the party has met them.

monster.description: The stat block they fight as.

notes.description: Who they are, from the world file.

NpcKnown.description: A place NPC the party has met, as a player sees them: never Hit Points, attitude or notes.

alive.description:
Whether they are alive, as far as the party knows: the party met them, so a death the
party saw is known.

id.description: The id; also their creature handle while the party is in their place.

OptionArea.description: The area an option fills, and a preview of each aim.

aims.description:
The creatures each aim would catch, allies included, for every creature and anchor of the
scene that catches at least one. An aim not listed here may still be submitted.

from_self.description:
Whether it starts at the actor (a cone, Thunderwave's cube): the aim then only points it.
Otherwise the aim is its centre, and must be within `range_ft`.

size_ft.description:
Its size in feet: a cone's or a line's length, a cube's side, a sphere's or a cylinder's
radius.

OptionId.description:
An action option's id, derived from the action and its context (weapon, spell and level),
never from a list index, e.g. `melee_attack/longsword`. Stable for the life of a prompt.

OptionItem.description: The item an option uses up.

id.description: Item id from the registry, as on the sheet, e.g. `potion_of_healing`.

remaining.description: How many the actor carries now, this one included.

concentration.description: Whether casting it starts Concentration, ending any Concentration the caster holds.

id.description: Spell id from the registry, as on the sheet, e.g. `bless`.

level.description: The level it is cast at: the slot it spends, or 0 for a cantrip.

Pace.description: How fast the party travels (SRD 5.2.1, Travel Pace).

oneOf.description: 2 miles an hour, 18 a day.
3 miles an hour, 24 a day.
4 miles an hour, 30 a day.

PlaceDm.description: A place as the DM sees it.

discovered.description: Whether the party has discovered it.

id.description: The place id.

inn_cp.description:
A night's room and board at its inn, per person, in copper pieces; absent when it has
no inn.

kind.description: What kind of place it is (`town`, `village`, `inn`, `ruin`).

scene.description: The scene the engine loads on arrival.

PlaceKnown.description: A discovered place, as a player sees it.

id.description: The place id; `travel` takes it as `to`.

inn_cp.description:
A night's room and board at its inn, per person, in copper pieces; absent when it has
no inn.

kind.description: What kind of place it is (`town`, `village`, `inn`, `ruin`).

oneOf.description: At one of the scene's anchors.
At an exact point.

PointFt.description: A point in feet. The engine works in metres internally and converts at the boundary.

_comment.description: Notes for humans reading the file. The engine ignores it.

equip.description: The slot it is worn or wielded in. Omitted: carried. Only a quantity of 1 can be equipped.

oneOf.description: Not proficient.
Proficient: adds the Proficiency Bonus.
Expertise: adds twice the Proficiency Bonus.

PromptId.description: A pending decision's id, e.g. `p57`. `submit`, `react` and `end_turn` echo it.

total_cp.description: Their worth in copper pieces, computed by the engine, so nobody at the table does sums.

ReachView.description:
How long one road out of the caravan's place takes (API-49), worked out by the world with the
travel rule: at a Normal pace, or the road's slower maximum, and when the day's distance runs
out on the way, a night on the road and on the next morning. Players read it as prose and a
watch; the minutes are for wording, never shown.

arrives.description: When the caravan gets to the road's other end.

minutes.description: Minutes on the move, nights left out.

nights.description: Nights spent before arriving: 0 when the caravan gets there today.

pace.description: The pace the plan goes at.

ReactionOption.description: A reaction the actor can take.

ReactionTrigger.description: The event that opened a reaction prompt.

event_seq.description:
The triggering event's `seq`: the mover's `moved` for an Opportunity Attack, and the
attacker's `action` for a reaction to an attack such as Shield. The attack roll itself is
logged only once the reaction is resolved, against the final AC.

summary.description: One plain sentence, e.g. "goblin_1 moves out of Bren's reach".

oneOf.description: At the start of each turn.
On a Short or Long Rest.
On a Long Rest.
Never on its own.

RejectReason.description: Why the engine refused a well-formed decision.

oneOf.description: The target is beyond the option's range.
No creature can be targeted by this option.
The chosen target cannot be targeted by this option.

The spawn is placed by the engine on its own trigger (a flag at combat start, or a

The spawn's creatures are already placed in this scene.
The actor lacks the skill proficiency the option needs (Help with a check).

The option uses up an item the actor no longer carries (a `use/<item>` option after the

The area option's aim catches no creature, so nothing is cast and nothing is spent.
The creature does not carry that item, or carries it only worn or wielded.
The purse holds less than the coins asked for, counted in copper with change.
`loot` of a creature that is neither down nor surrendered.
`loot` of a creature that carries nothing.
`place_creature` finds no free spot within 10 feet of where it was asked to place.

`travel` by someone who doesn't drive the caravan: not its owner, or not in the party
when an NPC owns it.

`travel` to a place or road no road from here leads to, or, without `to`, an NPC
owner's route with no next place.

`travel` at a pace faster than the road or the party allows; the message names the

`travel` after the day's distance is spent; a night's rest starts a new day.
`travel` while a wagon carries more than its limit.
`rest_night{where: inn}` where the caravan is not at a place with an inn.
`travel` or `rest_night` while a road card waits for its decision.
`choose_card` with no card on the table.

Request.description: One request line sent to the engine.

id.description: Client-unique request id. A repeated id returns the stored response and does not execute again.

viewer.description:
Who the response is for: `dm` or a creature handle. Selects the projection of every state,
sheet and event in the response (`contract/protocol.md` §5). A player agent's tools bind it
to that agent's own handle.

oneOf.description: Handshake: protocol name, versions and the schema hash. Clients refuse to start on a hash mismatch.
Starts a session: an empty log and no scene. Replaces any running session.

roster.description:
The party saved by an earlier session's `save_roster` (protocol §4.15). Each scene
pregen creature whose handle is in it is rebuilt as saved, after a Long Rest; a
campaign on the same map takes up its world.

seed.description:
Dice seed. The same seed and the same request stream give an identical log. When
omitted, the engine picks one and logs it in `session_started`; replaying with that
seed reproduces the session. Every value, 0 included, is a real seed.

oneOf.description:
Loads a scene from the scenario and enters explore mode, in the session's one engine.
Creatures in `party` carry over; every other creature of the previous scene leaves.
Refused with `wrong_mode` while a fight is running.

party.description:
Creatures carried in from the previous scene, with their HP, resources and conditions,
placed at the scene's `party_start` anchors in order (the last anchor takes any extra).
Empty for a scene that places its own creatures; required by a scene that places none.

scene_id.description: Scene id from the scenario file.

oneOf.description: The current state, projected for the request's `viewer`.

A creature's full sheet. Only its owner and `dm` may ask; anyone else gets `not_visible`.
Read-only: it rolls nothing and logs no event.

The options the actor can take at the pending action prompt. Only its owner and `dm` may
ask; anyone else gets `not_visible`. Returns `not_your_turn` when the engine is waiting on
someone else.

actor.description:
The creature whose options are listed. In explore mode any creature of the scene:
the options it could take on a turn of its own, as if that turn began now.

oneOf.description:
Takes one option at the pending action prompt, or, in explore mode, as a turn of the
actor's own.

actor.description: The acting creature; in combat it must be `awaiting.actor`.

aim.description:
Where an `area` option is aimed. Required for one; an aim that catches no creature is
rejected with `area_empty` and spends nothing.

option_id.description: One of the option ids `legal_actions` returned for this prompt.

point.description:
Target point, for options whose `targeting` is `point`. For an `area` option it means
the same as `aim: {kind: point}`.

prompt_id.description:
In combat, the pending prompt's id: required, and an old id is rejected with
`stale_prompt` and changes nothing. In explore mode leave it out; a submit that carries
one there is a late combat decision and answers `wrong_mode`.

targets.description: Targets, for options whose `targeting` is `single` or `multiple`.

variant.description: One of the option's `variants`, when it has any (e.g. a spell's casting level).

oneOf.description: Answers the pending reaction prompt.

choice.description: The `choice` of one of the prompt's options, or absent to decline.

oneOf.description: Ends the actor's turn.

Moves a creature along a route on the map. In explore mode the walk costs no movement
and provokes nobody. In combat it is a decision at the actor's action prompt: the whole
route must fit in the movement left, unless `partial` is set, and an opportunity attack
pauses the creature where it provoked one; it walks on once the reaction is resolved
(protocol §4.1). No route answers `rejected` with `no_path`.

partial.description:
Walk as far as movement allows: a route longer than the movement left is walked to
the last free spot the movement reaches, and the result's `reached` says it stopped
short. Without it (the default) such a move is refused with `insufficient_resource`
and changes nothing; so is a partial move that can't get anywhere. Ignored in explore
mode, where there is no movement to run out of.

prompt_id.description: The pending prompt's id. Required in combat, ignored in explore mode.

oneOf.description:
Asks the engine to roll an ability check or saving throw in explore mode. The engine rolls
and decides success, and applies the scenario check's consequences. Each scenario check is
rolled at most once per scene, by anyone; a second request answers `rejected` with
`already_attempted`. Advantage comes only from what the engine knows, never from the caller.

actor.description: The creature that makes the check.

oneOf.description:
A Short Rest, in explore mode only (rolling Initiative interrupts a rest, so combat
answers `wrong_mode`). Every participant needs at least 1 Hit Point (`rejected` with
`condition_prevents` otherwise). Each one spends the Hit Point Dice `hit_dice` gives it,
then short-rest resources recharge. A refused rest changes nothing.

hit_dice.description:
Hit Point Dice to spend per participant, declared up front. A participant not listed
spends none.

participants.description: The creatures that rest, each listed once.

oneOf.description:
Starts one of the scene's encounters: rolls initiative for its participants and enters
combat mode. Participants, surprise, surrender and end reasons come from the scene file,
never from the caller (decision D4). When the encounter's surprise flag is set, the
surprised side rolls initiative with Disadvantage.

encounter_id.description: Encounter id from the scene file.

oneOf.description:
Ends the running fight early, only for a reason its encounter allows: `surrender` while
its surrender condition holds, `scenario` when it lists that end reason. A fight that ends
by itself (a side is down) needs no `end_combat`: the scene is already back in explore mode.

Places the creatures of a spawn the scene declares `when: dm`, each at its own placement.
A spawn is placed at most once per scene (`rejected` / `already_spawned`); one the engine
places on its own trigger answers `rejected` / `automatic`. During a fight the creatures
join it: each rolls initiative and acts at its place in the order, this round if its
count has not come up yet, otherwise from the next. A pending prompt keeps its id. After a
fight they join a later one only if its encounter lists them.

spawn_id.description: Spawn id from the scene file.

oneOf.description:
The Help action in explore mode; in combat Help is one of the `legal_actions` options.
The helper must be conscious and within 5 feet of the other creature (`rejected` /
`out_of_range` otherwise; `move` there first). The `action` event, the Medicine roll of a
stabilize and any `life_state` change are in `events`. Combat answers `wrong_mode`.

help.description: What kind of help, and for whom.

oneOf.description: Log entries after `since`, projected for the request's `viewer`.

since.description: The `seq` to read after; `0` reads from the start.

oneOf.description:
Hands coin or one carried item to a creature within 5 feet, in explore mode (protocol
§4.9). The giver pays coin with change, as core makes it; the receiver gets the coins
named. Logs one public `ledger` entry with reason `trade`.

Tries to take coin or one carried item from a creature within 5 feet without being seen,
in explore mode (protocol §4.9). The engine rolls the thief's Dexterity (Sleight of Hand)
against the target's passive Perception. On a success the goods move, with a `ledger`
entry (reason `theft`) only the thief and the DM see; on a failure nothing moves and the
public `theft_noticed` says the target caught the thief.

Takes everything a fallen or surrendered creature within 5 feet carries, in explore mode
(protocol §4.9): its coins and items, one public `ledger` entry each, reason `loot`.

Places one monster the scene file doesn't list, for a story beat no authored spawn fits
(API-33, decision 0035; protocol §4.10). The DM's command: the game's DM tool takes the
stat block and its `carries` from the pack's `stat_blocks` list, never from the DM's own
words. The engine refuses an unknown stat block, a taken handle and an anchor the scene
doesn't have, and puts the creature on the nearest free spot within 10 feet of `at`. The
creature takes `side` whatever its faction: the engine sets attitudes to match (MON-11).
During a fight it joins it, as a spawn does. It is gone with the scene, like the scene's
own creatures.

at.description: Where it is placed: an anchor of this scene or a point.

carries.description: Coin and items it carries, from the pack's `stat_blocks` entry. DM-only until looted.

handle.description: A new handle, unique in the session and the scene's spawns: a plain name, not `dm`.

monster.description: A stat block id, as in a scene file's `monster` (`bandit`, or a namespaced id).

name.description: A display name instead of the stat block's, such as `Grey-coated bandit`.

side.description: Which side of a fight it is on.

oneOf.description:
Starts a fight no authored encounter fits, among creatures present (API-34, decision
0035; protocol §4.4). The DM's command, and the one exception to "participants come from
the scene file". Each participant must be in the scene, conscious and on the party or the
hostile side, listed once; at least one of each side. Initiative is rolled as for an
authored fight, with no surprise, no surrender condition and no early end: it ends when
a side is down. The fight is listed in the DM's `encounters` as `fight_<n>`.

participants.description: Every creature in the fight, in any order.

oneOf.description:
Starts the living world from the scenario pack's `campaign.json` (API-41; protocol
§4.11): its map, goods, start place, day and hour, caravan and route. Called once, by the
game loop as `dm`, after the start place's scene is loaded. The party is carried into
every scene a journey loads, as `load_scene` carries it.

human.description:
The human's creature, when a human plays: it breaks a tied Blade vote on a road
card (protocol §4.13).

party.description: The party: every creature in the current scene that travels with the caravan.

oneOf.description:
Travels one leg along one road (API-41; protocol §4.11). Only the caravan's owner, or any
party member when an NPC owns it, may call it, as themselves: never `dm`. The leg goes as
far as the day's distance allows and stops on the road when it is spent; the clock moves
on, core's time with it, and the engine loads the place's scene on arrival or the road
scene on the road, with the party.

actor.description: Who calls it: the viewer's own creature.

pace.description:
The pace; no faster than the road allows, and Slow when a party member's Speed is
halved.

to.description:
A neighbouring place id or a road id. Left out: on along the road, or to the next
place on the route when an NPC owns the caravan.

oneOf.description:
Spends the night (API-42; protocol §4.12): at the inn of the place the caravan is in, or
in camp. The day ends (food and the Malnutrition save through core), the party takes a
Long Rest through core, the clock moves to dawn and a new day of travel starts. The same
callers as `travel`: the caravan's driver, as itself, never `dm`.

actor.description: Who calls it: the viewer's own creature.

oneOf.description:
Speaks on the road card on the table (API-43; protocol §4.13): a Hired Blade's advice
on a caravan card or vote on a Blade card, or a player owner's call on a caravan card
once every Blade has advised. As the actor itself, never `dm`.

actor.description: Who speaks: the viewer's own creature.

oneOf.description:
Saves the party for the next game session (API-45; protocol §4.15): the campaign's
party, else every party character built from a pregen, and the world. DM only.

Opens a level-up (API-44; protocol §4.14) for a character whose sheet says
`xp.can_level_up`, out of combat. Core applies the new level and answers what has one
answer; the result carries the first choice left for the player, if any. Sent again while
the level-up is open, it returns the open choice. As the actor itself, never `dm`.

actor.description: Who levels up: the viewer's own creature.

oneOf.description: Answers the open level-up choice (API-44; protocol §4.14). As the actor itself.

actor.description: The levelling creature: the viewer's own.

picks.description: Option ids, as many as the choice's `picks`. Empty takes the choice's `recommended`.

id.description: Resource id, e.g. `fighter.second_wind`.

recharge.description: When every expended use comes back.

short_rest_regain.description:
Expended uses a Short Rest gives back when `recharge` is `long_rest`, e.g. 1 for Second
Wind. Absent when a Short Rest gives none back.

Response.description: One response line written by the engine, answering exactly one [`Request`].

awaiting.description: Who the engine waits on next. Never projected away: everyone may know whose turn it is.

error.description: Why the command failed. Set when `ok` is false.

events.description: The log entries this request produced, projected for the request's `viewer`. Empty on error.

id.description: The request id this answers; `null` only when the request line was too malformed to read an id.

log_head.description: The session log length after this request; pass it to `events.since` to read on from here.

ok.description: `true` when the command succeeded and `result` is set; `false` when `error` is set.

result.description: The command's result, tagged by the same `cmd` as the request. Set when `ok` is true.

oneOf.description: A Short Rest.
A Long Rest.

RoadDm.description: A road as the DM sees it.

good_road.description: Whether it is a good road (the maximum pace is one step faster).

id.description: The road id.

max_pace.description: The fastest pace the road allows.

to.description: The other end, a place id.

zone.description: The deck zone road cards come from.

RoadKnown.description: A road between two discovered places, as a player sees it.

good_road.description: Whether it is a good road.

id.description: The road id; `travel` takes it as `to`.

max_pace.description: The fastest pace the road allows.

reach.description:
How long the road takes from where the caravan stands (API-49): set on each road out of
the caravan's place, absent elsewhere and on the road.

to.description: The other end, a place id.

RoadUnexplored.description:
A road from a discovered place to one the party has not found yet, as a player sees it:
where it starts and how long it is, not where it leads.

from.description: The discovered end, a place id.

good_road.description: Whether it is a good road.

id.description: The road id; `travel` takes it as `to`.

max_pace.description: The fastest pace the road allows.

reach.description:
How long the road takes from where the caravan stands (API-49): set on each road out of
the caravan's place, absent elsewhere and on the road.

RollId.description: A roll's id, `r` plus a number, e.g. `r412`. Unique for the whole session, never reused.

oneOf.description: An attack roll.
A saving throw.
An ability check without a skill.
An ability check with a skill.
Initiative.
Damage.
Healing.
A death saving throw.
A roll on a world table, such as a road card draw. Its roller is `world`.
An attack hit.
An attack hit with a natural 20.
An attack missed.
A check or save succeeded.
A check or save failed.
A roll with nothing to compare, such as damage or initiative.
Everything the engine knows about the roll. The audit runs on this view.

advantage_sources.description:
The rules reasons behind `advantage`, as the engine tracked them, e.g. a condition or
a feature. Empty when the roll is normal.

against.description:
The number the total was compared with: always present for `attack` (AC),
`saving_throw`, `death_save`, `ability_check` and `skill_check` (DC); absent for
`initiative`, `damage` and `healing`.

dc_source.description: Where the DC came from: present on every check and save.

id.description: Session-unique roll id.

label.description: Short label, e.g. "Longsword attack vs goblin_1".

oneOf.description: What another player sees: the dice, the total and the result.

id.description: Session-unique roll id.

label.description: Short label, e.g. "Longsword attack vs goblin_1".

Roster.description: A party saved between game sessions.

characters.description: The party's characters, in party order.

world.description:
The world as the engine left it: the clock, where the caravan is, its wagons and cargo,
the places discovered, the deck. Absent when no campaign ran. Opaque to clients: give it
back unchanged.

RosterCharacter.description:
One character as it left a game session: a pregen with a history. Hit Points are not kept;
the next session starts after a Long Rest.

choices.description: The answers given in play to the level-up choices past the pregen's level.

days_without_food.description: Days in a row it has eaten nothing.

equipment.description: What it carries, equipped items with their slot.

handle.description: Its handle, which a scene's pregen creature of the same handle takes on.

malnutrition.description:
How many of those levels malnutrition caused: a Long Rest can't remove them until it
eats a full day's food.

pregen.description: The pregen file it was built from.

RosterChoice.description: One level-up choice answered in play.

level.description: The level it was made at.

picks.description: The option ids picked, as `level_up` listed them.

RosterWorld.description: The world part of a roster.

map.description:
The world map's id, e.g. `wend`. A campaign on another map starts fresh, and so does one
whose saved escort contract is done: the party keep their characters and take the
campaign's contract again from its start.

state.description: The world's state, as the engine wrote it.

Sheet.description: A creature's full sheet. Only its owner and the DM receive it.

abilities.description: The six abilities with their saving throws, Strength to Charisma.

class.description: Class id, e.g. `fighter`. Absent for monsters.

concentration.description: The spell it is concentrating on, if any.

conditions.description:
Active conditions, by name. A creature at 0 Hit Points that is not dead is
`unconscious`.

death_saves.description: Death saving throws so far, while unconscious.

effects.description:
Lasting effects on it that run out or end, such as Bless or a Help's Advantage, in the
order they began. Features that last for good are in `features` instead.

equipment.description:
Equipped items in slot order (armor, then weapons), then carried items in the order they
were picked up.

features.description:
Feats, then features granted by class, subclass, species and background (as actions,
e.g. Second Wind, or as lasting effects), each once.

hit_dice.description:
Hit Point Dice by die size, smallest first: one die per class level, spent on a short
rest. Empty for a creature without Hit Point Dice, such as a monster.

passive_perception.description:
Passive Perception, as core computes it (SRD 5.2.1): 10 plus the Perception bonus, plus 5
with Advantage on Perception checks or minus 5 with Disadvantage.

resources.description:
Limited-use features, e.g. Second Wind, by id. Per-turn action economy (action, bonus
action, reaction) is not listed; `legal_actions` reports it.

skills.description: The eighteen skills, in alphabetical order.

species.description: Species id for characters, creature type for monsters.

spell_slots.description: Spell slots by level; empty for non-casters.

spellcasting.description: One line per class with the Spellcasting feature; empty for non-casters.

spells.description:
Spells it can cast or prepare: cantrips, then levelled spells by level, each by name.
A class that prepares from its entire list (the Cleric) lists only what is prepared.

xp.description: Experience Points and whether the next level is due. Absent for monsters.

SheetConcentration.description: The spell a creature is concentrating on.

Side.description: Which side of a fight a creature is on, as seen by the party.

oneOf.description: The player characters and their allies.
